draft.change: Add a personal-name article for נֹחַ linked to the root article nuach.
draft.definition: Noah, the son whom Lamech names in hope of relief from toil.
draft.evidence: Genesis 5:29 gives the name נֹחַ and explains it through the wordplay on יְנַחֲמֵנוּ, “he will comfort us.”

analysis.evidence: The verse names Shem, Ham, and Japheth as the sons of נֹחַ who came out of the ark, identifying their father as Noah.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew proper noun with no prefix or suffix. It completes the construct phrase בְנֵי נֹחַ, “the sons of Noah.”

analysis.evidence: מִן הַתֵּבָה identifies the ark as the place from which Noah’s sons came out.
analysis.morphology: The definite article הַ precedes a Qal active participle in the masculine plural absolute. The participle modifies בְנֵי נֹחַ, “Noah’s sons.”
analysis.sense: go out, depart from a place or someone’s presence

analysis.evidence: In הַיֹּצְאִים מִן הַתֵּבָה, “who came out of the ark,” מִן marks the ark as the place Noah’s sons left.
analysis.morphology: Independent Hebrew preposition with no prefix or suffix.

draft.change: Add Genesis 9:18 as an example of the existing ark sense.
draft.definition: A vessel built to keep its occupants afloat on water.
draft.evidence: Genesis 9:18 identifies Shem, Ham, and Japheth as the sons of Noah who came out of the ark.

analysis.evidence: Genesis 9:18 describes Noah’s sons as הַיֹּצְאִים מִן הַתֵּבָה, “those who came out of the ark.” The preposition מִן identifies the ark as the vessel they left.
analysis.morphology: The definite article הַ precedes a feminine singular common noun in the absolute state.
analysis.sense: The vessel in which Noah and his family survived the flood.

analysis.evidence: After בְנֵי נֹחַ introduces Noah’s sons who came out of the ark, שֵׁם וְחָם וָיָפֶת lists them by name. שֵׁם is the first son named, alongside Ham and Japheth. The source gloss “Paran” is incorrect.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew proper noun with no prefix or suffix.

draft.change: Clarify the existing Genesis 9:18 evidence note by identifying Ham’s place in the list at the first occurrence.
draft.definition: Ham, son of Noah and father of Cush, Mizraim, Put and Canaan.
draft.evidence: Genesis 9:18 first names Ham among Noah’s sons and then identifies him as Canaan’s father.

analysis.evidence: The marked וְחָם stands between שֵׁם and וָיָפֶת in the list of בְנֵי נֹחַ, the sons of Noah who came out of the ark. The verse then repeats Ham’s name and identifies him as אֲבִי כְנָעַן, the father of Canaan.
analysis.morphology: The conjunction וְ, “and,” prefixes the personal name חָם and joins it to שֵׁם in the list of Noah’s sons.
analysis.sense: Ham, son of Noah and father of Canaan

analysis.evidence: The verse lists the sons of Noah who came out of the ark. וָיָפֶת names the third son in the list, after Shem and Ham.
analysis.morphology: The conjunction וָ means “and.” יָפֶת is the pausal form of the personal name יֶפֶת.

draft.change: Retain the current personal-name article. Its Genesis 9:18 note already explains the repeated name.
draft.definition: Ham, son of Noah and father of Canaan.
draft.evidence: In Genesis 9:18, הוּא refers back to the repeated חָם and אֲבִי כְנָעַן identifies him as Canaan’s father.

analysis.evidence: After listing Noah’s sons, the verse repeats Ham’s name in וְחָם הוּא אֲבִי כְנָעַן, “and Ham was the father of Canaan.”
analysis.morphology: The conjunction וְ introduces a new clause. The personal name חָם is its subject, resumed by the masculine singular pronoun הוּא.
analysis.sense: Ham, son of Noah and father of Canaan

analysis.evidence: In וְחָם הוּא אֲבִי כְנָעַן, הוּא links the subject חָם to the predicate אֲבִי כְנָעַן, “the father of Canaan.” The clause identifies Ham as Canaan’s father.
analysis.morphology: Independent third-person masculine singular pronoun agreeing with חָם. It has no prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: is (in a clause without a verb)

analysis.evidence: Carried forward: this word and its source tagging were reviewed identically at 66581:5, 66580:6.
וְחָם הוּא אֲבִי כְנָעַן means “and Ham was the father of Canaan.” The construct form אֲבִי identifies Canaan as Ham’s son.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew proper noun in pausal form, with no prefix or suffix.
